title: UI thread performs whole-buffer terminal reads under the pump's ioLock; selection copy issues one Rebex call per row
existing_state: Clipboard and scrollback actions run synchronously on the UI thread while holding the same ioLock the pump contends for: Copy All (system menu, Forms/InteractiveTerminalForm.cs:242-244, 488-507) invokes BuildClipboardText which pulls the entire history+screen region (up to 10,036 rows at the hardcoded 10k scrollback) in one GetRegionText call under ioLock (Services/Terminal/InteractiveTerminalService.cs:892-901 wiring, 3471-3495 implementation); Clear Scrollback copies and rewrites the visible screen cell-by-cell (cols x rows SetCell calls) under the same lock (3543-3576). Worst is drag-select auto-copy (fires on every mouse-up): BuildSelectionClipboardText calls screen.GetRegionText once per selected row (3516-3538), so selecting a few thousand scrollback rows issues thousands of individual Rebex region calls on the UI thread while the 2ms-cadence pump holds/contends the lock — a perceptible freeze on large selections during heavy output.
recommendation: In BuildSelectionClipboardText, fetch the full-width row span in a single GetRegionText(0, startSourceRow, columns, rowCount) call (the pattern BuildClipboardText already uses) and slice the first/last rows' columns in memory — one lock acquisition, one Rebex call. Optionally move Copy All's buffer read onto a worker task that takes the lock off the UI thread and sets the clipboard via BeginInvoke.
user_benefit: Selecting or copying large scrollback regions during active output no longer stutters the window or stalls the terminal pump.
